title: His brother, and piano lessons as a neighborhood custom
summary: Basie had an older brother he barely knew; his mother had a class of children, and the kids went to Mowchow or Holloway.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. All right. Can I ask you about, you know, I mean, do you have sisters and brother?
No.
You, (inaudible) --
Well, I had one brother. I did have one brother, but I knew very little about him. I mean, tell you, they lost him when I was just barely could remember.
I see.
No sisters. (inaudible)
He was older than you?
Yeah.
Yeah? I see. And, I mean, were people playing a lot of piano in your house?
No, no, nobody.
I mean, people come by or anything like that?
Anybody come by to play piano?
Yeah.
No, not really. Because, I mean, see, the piano was not important. Who thought about it? Unless they went to a dance or heard someone play (inaudible) or something (inaudible) or something like that.
But I mean, it was important enough for your mother to want you to take lessons.

Well, she -- yeah, she wanted me to take lessons, but whether she was thinking about anything as far as the future's concerned as far as music as being the thing, I don't think she (inaudible). She just thought I should have piano lessons and I think there's an awful lot of -- I know there were a lot of children. She had a regular class, and (inaudible) a lot of kids would come. They must have had some reason to take piano lessons.
Yeah.
I don't think they took piano lessons just
to be -- to make it (inaudible) have a career --
Uh-huh.

-- playing piano. They just took lessons. I mean, just like (inaudible) a lot of kids that could play a lot of things, you know, I mean, from the book, you know, with different numbers of the book, I mean, take lessons (inaudible). (Inaudible) some families that their parents (inaudible) take music lessons and they just be able to play (inaudible). That's because they have the background (inaudible) from one school, having music lessons --
Uh-huh.
-- like not going to school (inaudible) music lessons.
She went to her home, you mean, Grace Mowchow?
That's right.
Right.
That's where -- that's the way all the kids went there, either to her or a lady that I had by the name of (inaudible) Holloway. So there were two piano (inaudible), Holloway and Mowchows.
